title: Short-cycle parachute: pricing and hire-lag simulator
body:
Purpose: quick, short-cycle simulator to model emergency (parachute) price adjustments combined with hiring lag effects. Intended for ops + finance to evaluate 30–120 day outcomes when demand shifts and hires take time to onboard. Working spreadsheet (lightweight) — exploratory, assumptions explicit, no final approvals here.

### Tab: Overview
Date run: 2026-05-03
Owner: Aisha Rao
Status: draft / working hypotheses
Key outputs: 1) run-rate impact by scenario (30/60/90 day windows) 2) headcount addition schedule and lagged cost 3) nominal token elasticity / revenue sensitivity 4) trigger rules for automatic parachute pricing and hiring deceleration

### Tab: Assumptions (explicit)
- Base month ARR token-demand baseline: 18M tokens/day (~$540k MRR equivalent at current mix).
- Base blended price per 1k tokens: $0.030 (hosted avg)
- Elasticity by segment (point estimates): small-startups -0.9, mid-market -0.5, enterprise -0.15
- Mix: small-startups 40%, mid-market 40%, enterprise 20% of token volume
- Hiring cadence: new full FTE ramp cost = $18k/month loaded; time-to-impact (prod-ready) = 45 days median (sigma 10d)
- Burst reserve (pre-paid) covers 10% of peak demand for 14 days
- Quantization/cost-savings expected per model substitute: $0.006/token-equivalent saved on heavy requests if deployed (not immediate)

### Tab: Scenario table (rows are discrete experiments)
Columns: Scenario | Price delta (%) | Effective price after change ($/1k) | Expected demand delta (%) (weighted by elasticity) | 30d revenue delta (%) | 90d revenue delta (%) | Hiring add FTE planned | Hiring lag days | Near-term burn delta ($k/mo) | Notes
Rapid-parachute-high | +40% | =0.030*1.4 -> 0.042 | calc: weightedElastic(40%*-0.9,40%*-0.5,20%*-0.15) => -0.63*40%? (see formulas) | -12% | -6% | 8 | 45 | +144 | emergency price hike for capacity shortage
Soft-parachute-mid | +20% | 0.036 | mid elasticity -> ~-0.32 | -6% | -2% | 4 | 30 | +72 | target non-enterprise mix reduction, preserve enterprise
Regional-surge-brief | +15% in EU only | regional blended effect | demand shift internal routing +5% global | +3% (net) | +5% | 2 (localized) | 21 | +36 | short regional price floor |
No-price-hire-surge | 0% | 0.030 | demand +60% (product release) | +60% revenue short-term | +40% | 12 | hires queued but lagged 60 | +216 | more severe capacity spend, explore spot reserve
Quantize-first | -5% price but deploy quantization | 0.0285 | demand +2% | +1.8% | +3.5% | 0 | 0 | -18 | strategic trade: lower price but lower cost-per-token via quantization

NOTE: The table above is intentionally compact. Actual calculations use explicit weighted elasticity: WeightedElasticity = sum(segment_share * elasticity_segment). DemandDeltaPct ~= PriceDeltaPct * WeightedElasticity (approx linear over small deltas).
Formulas used in sheet (textual):
- WeightedElasticity = (0.4 * -0.9) + (0.4 * -0.5) + (0.2 * -0.15) = -0.54 (example)
- DemandDeltaPct = PriceDeltaPct * WeightedElasticity
- RevenueDeltaPct = (1 + PriceDeltaPct) * (1 + DemandDeltaPct) - 1
- Near-term burn delta ($k/mo) = HiringAddFTE * 18 (k/mo) + incremental GPU ops ($k) estimated as function of demand uplift * 0.02

### Tab: Headcount plan (ramp table)
Columns: Role | Quantity planned | Recruit lead time (days) | Offer to onboard (days) | Prod-ready days | Loaded cost ($k/mo) | Start date | Prod-ready date | Notes
Infra-engineer | 4 | 28 | 14 | 45 | 18 | 2026-05-10 | 2026-06-24 | expedite with contract-to-hire pool
SRE | 3 | 21 | 10 | 35 | 20 | 2026-05-15 | 2026-06-19 | prioritize regional capacity
Support-engineer (oncall) | 6 | 14 | 7 | 21 | 12 | stagger start 2026-05-20 | rolling | use temp staffing early
Cost math notes: prod-ready date = start date + prod-ready days; first-month productivity scaled by 0.6 for partial month; full load from month 2.

### Tab: Trigger rules (workbook logic / decision matrix)
- If system P95 latency > 1.5x SLA for > 3h AND available reserved capacity < 12% for next 24h -> trigger Rapid-parachute-high pricing + activate hiring freeze exception for immediate contractors.
- If volume > baseline*1.25 sustained > 7d -> open hiring tranche (size = ceiling((volumeIncreasePct * baselineToken)/avgTokensPerFTE)) with priority tag 'surge'.
- If revenue delta negative > 8% after price hike -> rollback to previous price within 7d and enable targeted enterprise discounts to retain customers.
- If hiring lag > 45 days AND on-call incidents > 2x baseline -> escalate to exec ops and consider temporary region-exclusive price uplift.

### Tab: Sensitivity slice (select outputs)
- Sensitivity A: Elasticity variation +/- 20% -> revenue outcomes change materially for rapid hikes. Example: with elasticity -0.65 revenue drop after +40% price = -16% vs with -0.43 -> -8% (approx).
- Sensitivity B: Hiring lag variation +/- 14 days -> burn and capacity gap: 14d longer lag increases overtime/contract spend by ~18% per tranche.
- Sensitivity C: Mix shift (enterprise share +10ppt) -> effective elasticity moves from -0.54 to -0.39, reducing demand drop on price hikes by ~28%.

### Tab: Quick visual sketches (text for charts)
Chart 1: 30/60/90 day revenue delta stacked bars for scenarios (Rapid-parachute-high, Soft-parachute-mid, No-price-hire-surge).
Chart 2: Headcount ramp Gantt (start vs prod-ready) with shading for partial productivity months.
Chart 3: Break-even price increase by elasticity bucket (line chart).

### Tab: Playbook & operations notes
- Immediate: share this sheet with oncall leads + recruiting to validate realistic lead times.
- 48h: run a focused seat-of-pants calc in staging to confirm latency -> price trigger mapping.
- 5d: if parachute triggered, schedule customer comms templates (enterprise carve-outs ready).
- 14d: revisit quantization rollouts for hotspots (if present) as cost-mitigation to avoid repeated price hikes.

### Open questions / TODOs
- Validate enterprise elasticity empirically (run a small regional price A/B on 3% of EU traffic).
- Confirm contract-to-hire supplier capacity and typical ramp from offer -> prod-ready for infra roles.
- Re-run model including GPU spot market pricing sensitivity (linked doc: JIRA-FIN-4523).

Quick reference formulas (paste into spreadsheet):
- Cell E2 (WeightedElasticity): =SUMPRODUCT(segment_share_range, elasticity_range)
- Cell F2 (DemandDeltaPct): =PriceDeltaPct * E2
- Cell G2 (RevenueDeltaPct): =(1+PriceDeltaPct)*(1+F2)-1
- BurnDelta: =HiringAddFTE * loaded_cost_k + (VolumeChangeTokens * cost_per_token_ops)

Authorship note: draft authored by Aisha Rao (finance-ops). Marcus Villanueva (recruiting estimates), Priya Singh (go-to-market elasticity inputs), Ellen Park (ops latency triggers) contributed.

Last update: 2026-05-10 — awaiting recruitment validation and empirical elasticity tests.
